common_gate.name: finite obstruction module
common_gate.requirement: Construct a finite module E over a commutative Noetherian coefficient ring A, its boundary ideal I, and a finite presentation when a colon certificate is intended.

common_gate.name: localized vanishing
common_gate.requirement: Prove that the distinguished defect vanishes outside V(I), using localized corrections and conductor compatibility when corrections are constructed on normalization charts.

common_gate.name: positive relative height
common_gate.requirement: Prove that no minimal component of Supp(E) is contained in V(I).

common_gate.name: no embedded boundary support
common_gate.requirement: Prove that E is S1, or directly that no associated prime of E contains I.

common_gate.name: support saturation
common_gate.requirement: Conclude H_I^0(E)=0, equivalently N:I^infinity=N for a presentation E=F/N, and only then kill the defect.

cubic-keller.target: H_I^0(Q)=0 and N:I^infinity=N; together with T=T^[2], obtain cotangent cyclicity and point-flatness.

not_applicable_gates.reason: The cubic path proves the entire module H_I^0(Q) vanishes rather than killing one preconstructed defect class, so no separate localized-vanishing certificate is needed.

model_frontiers.scope: The complete deterministic quartic nongauge complements for the six singular squarefree cubic symbols.
model_frontiers.C1: fails on every geometric fiber of every displayed full complement family by a parameter-independent multiplicity-six Ext^2 support-hull obstruction
model_frontiers.C2: passes on every geometric fiber by strict Rees base change from the saturated central cotangent presentation
model_frontiers.programme_effect: Fiberwise base change is closed on the complete quartic complement families. The global Keller-compatible C1 and C2 gates remain open because higher formal orders, normality, and Keller-open compatibility are not supplied.

stages.requirement: Use Proposition 1.17's finite presentation of Q and the collision ideal I.

Prove T -> T^[2] is onto; then Q has pure two-dimensional full support and the finite collision locus has relative height at least two. Under a Cartier Kähler different, Proposition 1.15a identifies this with Cohen--Macaulayness of the local normalization.
Prove Q is S1, or give an equivalent associated-prime, regular-element, Cohen--Macaulay/perfect, or direct-colon certificate.
Apply SST1 after C1 and C2; Proposition 1.16 then identifies the primitive-conormal defect with H_I^0(Q).

failure_routes: If T -> T^[2] is not onto, retain the nonzero support-hull defect L=C/T.
If a minimal component of Supp(Q) lies in V(I), support saturation cannot remove it.
If an embedded associated prime contains I, extract its I-supported torsion class instead of invoking SST1.

plane-jc.module: M=coker(Phi) for the conductor/gauge-jet matching map
plane-jc.support_ideal: I_Z defining the finite surviving Case-1 stratum Z
plane-jc.target: rho in H_Z^0(M), followed by H_Z^0(M)=0.

stages.requirement: Compile the actual finite matching map Phi and prove its conductor/contact-loss truncation is independent of omitted Newton bands.
Construct rho in coker(Phi) and prove rho vanishes away from Z, including vanishing of any divisorial relative-different defect before forming a finite-support class.
Prove Z contains no minimal component of Supp(M); a nonzero module supported entirely on Z fails this gate.
Prove M is S1 or certify associated-prime avoidance/direct presentation saturation.
Apply SST1 after P0--P3 to conclude rho=0.

failure_routes: A surviving divisorial different defect means localized vanishing has not been reached.
If M is nonzero and supported entirely on Z, prove componentwise surjectivity of Phi or enlarge the coefficient family.
A nonzero associated prime over I_Z is an obstruction class, not a removable presentation artifact.

restricted-weyl.module: E_m=coker(d_{1,m}) or its strict Rees obstruction module
restricted-weyl.support_ideal: the boundary ideal b, or its homogeneous Rees lift J
restricted-weyl.target: vanishing of the global order-m obstruction after localized solution and conductor descent.

stages.requirement: Use the relative finite coherent obstruction module rather than only a fixed-symbol fiber matrix.
Solve the localized correction equation and supply conductor-compatible primitives. The certified all-pole degree-five obstruction does not satisfy this hypothesis.
For a filtered claim, prove strictness of the actual Rees correction, gauge, and mismatch maps and exclude unwanted t-torsion.
Prove that the boundary contains no minimal Fitting component of E_m or of the Rees obstruction module.
Prove S1 or direct associated-prime avoidance for the same module used in W2--W3.
Apply SST1 after W1--W4; for a bounded algebraic solution also supply the separate finite-tail effectivity hypothesis.

failure_routes: A class nonzero on the localized easy open is a genuine obstruction and is outside support saturation.
A Fitting component contained in the boundary fails relative height and must be analyzed as an exceptional component.
Failure of Rees strictness is a presentation/gauge mismatch; it cannot be removed by specializing to the associated graded module.
Boundary vanishing gives existence of a global correction but not finite filtration effectivity.
